conventions: Construct chains whose arthrous rectum the ASV renders with no determiner of its own give the phrase's single *the* to the rectum's article (rule 29 fronting) throughout the chapter, and this includes אִישׁ הָאֱלֹהִים → *the man of God* (8.14), where *God* is read as an anarthrous rendering of הָאֱלֹהִים and the construct keeps bare *man*; the same reading covers *the store cities* (8.4, 8.6), *the chief officers* (8.10), *the feast of unleavened bread / weeks / tabernacles* (8.13) and *the sea shore* (8.17).

The distributive repetitions דְבַר־יוֹם בְּיוֹם(וֹ) → *the duty of every day required* (8.13, 8.14) and לְשַׁעַר וָשָׁעַר → *at every gate* (8.14) are read under rule 22 with the first occurrence taking the noun and *every*, the second preposition, waw, noun and suffix unrepresented, and the supplied *required* its own added unit rather than folded into דְבַר; the *of* is the construct relation of דְבַר and goes to the first יוֹם as its rectum.

מֶלֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹה with the article → *king Solomon* leaves the article unrepresented (8.10, 8.18); הֵמָּה takes *they* where the ASV writes it (8.9), is unrepresented as a resumptive pronoun the relative already carries (8.7), and takes the lexical expression *the places* where the ASV writes that for it (8.11, margin 'Hebrew they are' read and set aside).
report: Read all 18 verses end to end against the 46-lemma candidate table and the added/unrepresented units the table cannot see. No construction is analysed two ways without the ASV licensing the difference.

Rule 29 fronting is applied uniformly wherever an arthrous rectum is rendered anarthrously: store cities (8.4, 8.6), chief officers (8.10), feast of unleavened bread / weeks / tabernacles (8.13), the man of God (8.14), the sea shore (8.17); and the arthrous count is applied uniformly where the ASV writes a determiner before the rectum's own word: courses of the priests (8.14), commandment of the king (8.15), cities for his chariots / horsemen (8.6, article → *his* under rule 41).

The two distributive repetitions (יוֹם בְּיוֹם in 8.13 and 8.14, לְשַׁעַר וָשָׁעַר in 8.14) are read identically under rule 22: first occurrence takes noun and *every*, repeated preposition/waw/noun/suffix unrepresented, and the supplied *required* is added in both verses.

הֵמָּה is treated three ways (8.7 unrepresented, 8.9 *they*, 8.11 *the places*) and each is licensed by what the ASV wrote; 'king Solomon' leaves the article unrepresented in both 8.10 and 8.18; the added units (*As for* 8.7, *of bondservants* 8.8, *even* 8.10 and 8.13, *required* 8.13/8.14, *So* 8.16, *them* 8.18) are each correctly placed and none is folded elsewhere in another verse.

BSB disagreements are all convention: object markers, prepositions silenced by ASV recasting (had/levy/servants/my/gerund/dative), resumptive pronoun and suffix, unwritten connectives, distributive repetitions, and articles the ASV does not write. No genuine error found.

Two single-verse choices were reviewed and left standing with their notes: 8.8 *of them* on the object suffix (rule 44 would put the *of* on the verb; the recasting demotes the suffix to a partitive adjunct rather than reaching it as object) and 8.13 חֳדָשִׁים → *new moons* headed on *new* under rule 31's ASV-usage tie-break. Neither touches another verse.
Nothing here generalises beyond the contract as written; no promotions or amendments.
